text:
maria: quick sync — i sketched a lightweight 'token-mux' layer that sits between ingress router and admission. idea: per-tenant mux can track soft-evict score + probe tickets, let router prefer healthy lanes. thoughts?
raj: curious — is this trying to decouple quota state from the admission service?
sophie: yes, and reduce cross-service lock contention. mux would keep ephemeral per-tenant counters and a small LRU for probes.
oliver: sounds plausible. what about correctness under scale? lease races are my worry.
maria: agreed. plan is staged leases: 1) optimistic increment in mux, 2) background reconcile with admission shard, 3) fast fallback on mismatch. keeps tail latency low.
raj: can you paste config sketch? would like to see time windows / probe budget.
maria: sure — minimal example:
```yaml
mux: 
  window_ms: 1000
  token_capacity: 1000
  probe_rate_per_tenant: 0.01  # probes per second
  soft_evict_threshold: 0.85
  reconcile_interval_ms: 200
```
kei: nit — probe_rate should be adaptive by tenant SLA. low-SLA tenants get fewer probes to avoid accidental evict.
sophie: agree. also need deterministic tie-breakers when two tenants hit same host slot (fairness). round-robin + weight is simple.
oliver: what about abuse signals? mux can incorporate recent 429/abuse flags from admission and temporarily lower capacity for a tenant. do we need a separate abuse pipeline?
raj: prefer small signal surface. mux should accept signed signals from admission: {tenant,score,expiry}. admission computes score from model of badbehaviour.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure mux runs stateless w/ sticky cache TTL < reconcile_interval, add metrics: mux_increments, reconcile_mismatches, probe_grants.
maria: good call. also thinking of a graceful decline policy: when host is overloaded, mux emits 'soft-evict' header so router can route to warm fallback variants.
kei: how would rollout look? start as read-only observer, emit guidance metrics for 2 weeks, then enable incremental control for low-traffic tenants.
sophie: testing plan: synthetic burst tests + mixed-tenant percentile SLOs. need chaos for reconcile RPCs failing.
raj: curious about storage — keep mux in-memory per-host or a shared, sharded cache? in-memory scales but complicates global rebalancing. shared store increases latency.
maria: prefer in-memory with gossip sync for long-lived tokens. reconcile ensures eventual consistency. we can later swap to sharded redis if needed.
oliver: ok but add deterministic eviction keys so two hosts won't both accept the same probe ticket. maybe include host-id in ticket HMAC.
maria: yep — ticket format: base64(hmac(host_id|tenant|nonce)|expiry). admission validates HMAC.
kei: operationally, we need metrics per-tenant: probe_accept_rate, mux_miss_rate, reconcile_lag. please add to design doc.
sophie: also add SLI for misrouted requests due to mux staleness. fallback must be safe.
raj: ACK. last question: will this change policy surface for product? do we need admin controls to lock tenants into dedicated mode?
maria: yes — admin API to pin tenant to dedicated pool or disable mux control. UI toggle for emergency.
infra-bot: note: security review required for HMAC key rotation and ticket replay protection.
maria: thanks all — i'll update the RFC with config defaults and rollout playbook. assigning follow-ups: @raj traffic sims, @sophie test harness, @kei ops metrics. :thumbsup:
